# vendor/orca.exe rebuild — 2026-09-11 (Claude Opus 5)

Task 6 audit finding **P1-07**: upstream ORCA's `main()` returned 0 after an
`init()` failure, and `init()` had already created the (empty) output file, so
the Python boundary in `influence/graphlets.py` — which tested
`returncode != 0 or not exists(fout)` — could not see bad-argument, unreadable
file, out-of-range id, self-loop or duplicate-edge failures. Only the row-count
backstop caught them, with a misleading message.

## Change to the vendored source

`vendor/orca.cpp`, `main()`: `return 0;` → `return 1;` on the init-failure
branch, with a comment block recording the change. **No counting code was
touched.**

## Build

```
/c/msys64/ucrt64/bin/g++ -O2 -std=c++11 -static -o vendor/orca.exe vendor/orca.cpp
g++.exe (Rev9, Built by MSYS2 project) 15.2.0
```

(the same command `verify_pipeline.py` prints when the binary is missing.)

## Evidence the counting output is unchanged

Orbit tables from the shipped binary and the rebuilt one compared with
`np.array_equal` (scratch `cmp_orca.py`, 2026-09-11 22:03 IST):

| graph | node gs=4 | edge gs=4 | node gs=5 | edge gs=5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ca-GrQc (n=4158, m=13422) | identical (4158×15) | identical (13422×12) | identical (4158×73) | identical (13422×68) |
| email-Eu-core (n=986, m=16064) | identical (986×15) | identical (16064×12) | identical (986×73) | identical (16064×68) |

Init-failure behaviour on a self-loop input: rebuilt binary rc=1, stderr
"Self loops … / Stopping!", 0-byte output; shipped binary rc=0 on the same input.
